title: Shower Valve Stem Replacement: Replacing a Worn Hot-Water Stem in a Three-Valve Faucet
summary: This This Old House episode documents diagnosing a temperature-fluctuating shower caused by a likely worn hot-water stem in a three-valve faucet. The host walks through exposing the stem assembly, removing the handle and escutcheon, backing out the bonnet, and evaluating wear. He demonstrates replacing the hot-stem unit and valve seat, using a seat wrench to extract the old seat, applying pipe-thread sealant, reinstalling the new stem with its bonnet, reusing bushings, sealing escutcheons with plumbers putty, and finally testing the hot water to confirm the repair works correctly.

sections.title: Diagnosis and valve identification
sections.description: The host identifies a three-valve setup (hot stem, cold stem, diverter) and points to the hot stem as the likely fault causing temperature drift when hot water is used.

sections.title: Accessing the stem and removing the handle
sections.description: To work on the stem, the index is pried off, the tub drain is blocked to prevent loss, and the Phillips screw behind the escutcheon is loosened to pull the handle off the stem.

sections.title: Removing the bonnet and assessing wear
sections.description: The bonnet is backed out from the valve inside the wall, and a socket wrench is used to loosen the outside nut. The stem unit is exposed and inspected for wear, with observation of looseness and milling precision indicating worn threads on older units.

sections.title: Replacement planning
sections.description: The host concludes that the hot stem threads are worn and plans to replace the stem and the seat, noting that the necessary parts are available.

sections.title: Replacing the valve seat using a seat wrench
sections.description: The old seat is removed with a seat wrench; the old seat is shown and the new one is prepared for installation, including applying pipe-thread sealant to the new threads.

sections.title: Installing new stem and bonnet
sections.description: The new stem unit with its bonnet and gasket is installed, and the assembly is tightened with the appropriate wrench.

sections.title: Rebuilding remaining components and sealing escutcheons
sections.description: The host explains rebuilding the remaining valve parts (diverter and cold side) and seals the escutcheons with plumbers putty, while reusing bushings to reinstall handles.

sections.title: Final test of hot-water operation
sections.description: The hot water is turned on and the repaired valve is shown to hold hot water consistently, confirming a successful repair.
